channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Malaysian Ringgit: Range-bound risks and key levels against US Dollar – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Christopher Wong notes that Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) kept the OPR at 2.75% and struck a slightly firmer tone, with growth expected to stay resilient into 2027. The economist still projects an OPR normalisation to 3.00% in January 2027.

item.title: USD/MXN Price Forecast: Peso rally targets April 2024 low
item.description: The Mexican Peso appreciates against the US Dollar, testing two-year highs near 16.85 as the USD/MXN sets aside a strong US Nonfarm Payrolls report, which was ignored by the Peso’s bears.

item.title: Malaysian Ringgit: BNM hawkish tilt supports MYR – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank highlights that Bank Negara Malaysia kept the OPR at 2.75% but shifted to a more hawkish bias, removing language that policy is "appropriate" and signalling vigilance on cost pressures.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: NFP rally stalls at 0.8100, retraces
item.description: The USD/CHF registers modest gains of over 0.30% as the Greenback is boosted by a solid US Nonfarm Payrolls report, pushing the pair above the 50-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) to reach a daily high of 0.8126. At the time of writing, trades at 0.8098.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah: Two-way risks around support levels – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Christopher Wong notes that USD/IDR has pulled back as a softer Dollar and lower UST yields support the Indonesian Rupiah. He highlights Bank Indonesia Governor Destry Damayanti’s emphasis on a stability-first approach, prioritizing Rupiah and macro stability while still supporting growth.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Services PMI rebound keeps PBoC cautious – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank says China’s August Services PMI rebound highlights some resilience in private-sector activity, but weak retail sales, soft inflation and higher unemployment still point to fragile domestic demand.

item.title: Sterling’s rally stalls as US jobs data reopens Fed debate
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) retreats some 0.09% against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday as the latest US inflation report reaffirmed Federal Reserve (Fed) Chair Kevin Warsh's view that the labor market is “consistent with full employment.” GBP/USD trades near the open at 1.3512.

item.title: Malaysia: Hawkish pause keeps options open – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economist Chua Han Teng notes that Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) held the Overnight Policy Rate at 2.75% while dropping language that the current level is appropriate. DBS expects rates to remain unchanged through 2026 but sees risks tilted towards a one-off policy normalisation.

item.title: Indian Rupee: Dollar inflows support INR but impulse may fade – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Christopher Wong notes that strong foreign-currency inflows linked to the RBI’s special measures have bolstered the Indian Rupee (INR) and strengthened the central bank’s FX buffer.

item.title: Eurozone: Inflation above target into 2027 – Nordea
item.description: Nordea expects Eurozone inflation dynamics to stay persistent, with headline inflation projected above the ECB’s target at least until spring 2027.

item.title: Fed’s Hammack says policy is not restrictive enough
item.description: Cleveland Federal Reserve (Fed) President Beth Hammack said on Friday that the current monetary policy stance is not restrictive, emphasizing that inflation is too high.

item.title: Turkey: CBRT likely to hold before two Q4 rate cuts - ING
item.description: ING’s Muhammet Mercan notes the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye (CBRT) has normalised liquidity via weekly repo auctions, bringing effective funding costs down to the 37% policy rate.

item.title: Australian Dollar resumes advance as US Dollar loses post-NFP momentum
item.description: AUD/USD resumes its advance on Friday after a brief bout of weakness following a stronger-than-expected United States (US) employment report.

item.title: Gold falls as traders increase Fed hawkish bets after stellar NFP
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) price retreats by about 0.80% on Friday, after registering losses of over 2% following the release of an upbeat US jobs report.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average falls on a jobs number the president loves
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average trades just short of 53,400, roughly 325 points or 0.6% lower on Friday, after August Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) printed 162K against a 56K forecast at 12:30 GMT and pushed the probability of a September hike above 60%.

item.title: Silver claws back post-NFP losses after briefly crashing below $65
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) trades around $66.20 at the time of writing on Friday, down 1.18% on the day, after recovering part of its sharp post-Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) decline.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Euro forms potential higher low above 100-day SMA
item.description: EUR/USD sees sharp two-way price swings on Friday after a stronger-than-expected United States (US) employment report triggers fresh volatility. The pair initially fell to an intraday low of 1.1585 before recovering as the US Dollar (USD) struggled to sustain its gains.

item.title: Brent: Questionable flows, fragile outlook – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Commodity Research team, led by Barbara Lambrecht, notes that uncertainty over crude flows through the Strait of Hormuz and conflicting transit data are clouding the outlook for Brent.

item.title: European Central Bank: Dovish hold may follow September hike - Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior Macro Strategist Bas van Geffen expects the European Central Bank (ECB) to hike its deposit rate by 25bp to 2.50% next week and then hold at that level for an extended period.

item.title: United States Dollar Index rises as strong NFP revives Fed hike bets
item.description: The United States Dollar Index (DXY) rises some 0.17% on Friday following a stellar Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) report, with the economy creating nearly three times as many jobs as expected by most economists, as reported by the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS).

item.title: Hungary: Inflation uptick complicates rate-cut path – ING
item.description: ING’s Peter Virovacz expects Hungarian industrial production to rebound in July, helping avoid a third-quarter GDP decline despite August headwinds from heatwave-related energy issues.

item.title: Gold recovers from post-NFP low as US Dollar trims gains
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) remains under pressure on Friday after stronger-than-expected United States (US) Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) data revive expectations of a Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike.

item.title: Swiss Franc loses ground upbeat US Nonfarm Payrolls
item.description: USD/CHF trades higher on Friday as stronger-than-expected United States (US) Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) data trigger fresh volatility. The pair jumped to 0.8126 following the release before giving back part of its advance. At the time of writing, USD/CHF trades around 0.8102, up nearly 0.34% on the day.

item.title: Canada: Gradual improvement outlook on labour market – RBC
item.description: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) economist Claire Fan notes Canada’s labour market lost 42,000 jobs in August, partly reversing earlier gains and leaving modest year-to-date job growth. She emphasizes structural factors like demographics and weaker immigration as key drags.

item.title: United States: Solid jobs data support steady Fed – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Dr. Christoph Balz notes that the U.S. labor market surprised to the upside in August, with Nonfarm Payrolls and private sector jobs both rising strongly while the unemployment rate held at 4.1%. Wage growth continued to slow.

item.title: European Central Bank: September hike path and oil risks – Nomura
item.description: Nomura’s Global Markets Research team, led by Andrzej Szczepaniak, George Buckley and Josie Anderson, expects the ECB to raise the depo rate by 25bp to 2.50% at the 10 September meeting and then pause.

item.title: "Lower the rate or I’ll stop trading": Trump pressures Fed after strong US jobs report
item.description: In a post on Truth Social, United States (US) President Donald Trump welcomed the creation of 162K jobs in August, a figure he described as significantly above expectations.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Jobs weakness caps gains against US Dollar - TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists note that Canada’s softer August labour report, including weaker employment momentum and slower wage growth, is unlikely to materially change the Bank of Canada’s (BoC) assessment of the labour market.

item.title: Canadian Dollar slides as Canada sheds 41.7K jobs, US payrolls surge
item.description: USD/CAD accelerates sharply higher on Friday, trading around 1.3850 at the time of writing, up 0.39% on the day.

item.title: US Dollar: Jobs strength lifts hike odds – ING
item.description: ING’s James Knightley notes that stronger-than-expected US August jobs data, with 162,000 new positions and upward revisions, has increased the perceived likelihood of a September Federal Reserve rate hike.
